title: Sample Clearance License
summary: License the use of a portion of an existing recording or song (a sample or interpolation) in a new track.
useWhen: An artist or producer used part of someone else's recording or composition and needs permission before release.
watchOuts: Sampling a recording usually requires two clearances: the master (from the label or owner) and the composition (from the publishers). Re-playing or re-singing a melody (interpolation) needs only the composition. Use this template once for each owner.
Clear before release. After release, owners have more leverage and may demand a larger share or a takedown.
Composition clearances often take a percentage of the new song's copyright. That reduces every writer's share, so update the split sheet.
There is no fixed length that is automatically 'fair use' or de minimis. U.S. courts disagree, especially for sampled recordings.

variables.label: Licensee
variables.help: Artist or label using the sample.

variables.label: Rights licensed
variables.help: Use one agreement per owner and right.

variables.label: Original work sampled
variables.help: Title, artist and writers, and recording year.

variables.label: Portion used
variables.help: Timestamp, length, and how it is used (looped, chopped, re-sung).

variables.label: New work
variables.help: Title and artist of the new track.

variables.label: Ongoing participation
variables.help: Master licenses often take a royalty. Publishing licenses often take a share of the new song.

variables.label: Royalty or share (%)
variables.help: Percent of net master income, or percent ownership of the new composition.

variables.label: Credit
variables.default: Contains a sample of [title] by [artist], courtesy of [owner]

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 2. Sample
sections.body: Original work: {{source}}. Rights licensed: {{rights}}. Portion used: {{portion}} (the "Sample"). New work: {{new_work}} (the "New Work").

sections.title: 3. License
sections.body: On payment of {{fee}}, Rights owner grants Licensee a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual license to use the Sample in the New Work, including its versions (clean, instrumental, sped-up or slowed, and approved remixes), and to exploit the New Work in all media, except that synchronization in advertising or political content needs separate approval.

sections.title: 4. Royalty on the new master
sections.body: Licensee will pay Rights owner {{royalty_value}}% of Licensee's net income from the New Work master, accounted twice a year with statements, with an annual audit right.

sections.title: 5. Share of the new composition
sections.body: Rights owner will own {{royalty_value}}% of the copyright in the New Work's composition, and will register its share with its PRO and The MLC. The other writers' shares are reduced accordingly. Licensee will deliver an updated split sheet. Licensee: [[initial:licensee]]

sections.title: 6. Credit
sections.body: Licensee will credit: "{{credit}}" in metadata and liner notes where credits appear.

sections.title: 7. Limits
sections.body: The license covers only the Sample as described, in the New Work. Using more of the original work, or using it in another work, needs a new license. Licensee will not use the original artist's name to imply endorsement.

sections.title: 8. Promises
sections.body: Rights owner owns or controls the {{rights}} rights in the Sample and may grant this license. This license does not cover rights owned by others, such as the other side of the copyright, or featured performers' consents where required.

sections.title: 9. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Rights owner** — {{licensor_name}}

[[sig:licensor]]

Printed name: [[name:licensor]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:licensor:Title]]
Date: [[date:licensor]]

**Licensee** — {{licensee_name}}

[[sig:licensee]]

Printed name: [[name:licensee]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:licensee:Title]]
Date: [[date:licensee]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Music rights are split between the composition (song) and the sound recording (master); royalties also depend on PRO, publisher, distributor and label agreements that this template does not change. An entertainment attorney should review deals involving advances, ownership transfers or long terms.
